marks.gloss_en: מה נפשך: if [the half-olives] combine, let him be flogged for cooking too; if they do not combine, let him not be flogged for eating either -- either way Rav's two rulings should agree
לעולם לא מצטרפי, ובבא מיורה גדולה -- they do not combine, and the eating-liability is where it comes from a large pot (= p_ba_miyora_gedola)
actually they do not combine, and [the eating is] where it comes from a large pot
דאמר קרא: לא תבשל גדי בחלב אמו (Deut 14:21) -- the kid, not the milk
(stam, first answer) there it is different, for the verse says 'you shall not cook a kid in its mother's milk' -- the Torah forbade the kid, and not the milk
וכן תני לוי במתניתין: כשם שלוקה על אכילתו כך לוקה על בישולו
Levi: he is flogged for cooking it too
דתניא: טפת חלב שנפלה על החתיכה... (R' Yehuda, Chachamim, and Rebbi's placement of their words) -- the marker is דתניא, not תניא נמי הכי
stam: and efshar lesochato itself is [a dispute of] tannaim
אלא לעולם קסבר רב חלב נמי אסור, והכא במאי עסקינן -- כגון שנפל לתוך יורה רותחת, דמבלע בלע מפלט לא פליט (= p_yora_rotachat)
(stam, surviving answer) rather, Rav holds the milk too is forbidden, and here we deal with where it fell into a boiling pot: it absorbs, it does not expel
וסבר רב גדי אסרה תורה ולא חלב? והא איתמר: חצי זית בשר וחצי זית חלב... לוקה על אכילתו -- if the kid only, why is he flogged for eating? it is half a measure!
half an olive-bulk of meat and half an olive-bulk of milk that he cooked together -- Rav: he is flogged for eating it
סוף סוף כי נייח הדר פליט! -- in the end, when it settles, it expels
כשקדם וסילקו -- where he removed it first
ואלא לא ניער בתחלה אלא בסוף... אמאי? הא בלע והא פלט! -- why should R' Yehuda's forbidding be correct there?
reading: he did not stir at first but at the end, and did not cover at first but at the end
קסבר אפשר לסוחטו אסור -- [Rebbi] holds an item that can be wrung out is forbidden (attribution to rebbi of p_els_asur)
מבלע בלע, מפלט לא פליט -- it absorbs and does not expel, so [R' Yehuda's forbidding all] cannot be meant there
reading: he did not stir at all and did not cover at all
Chachamim: [it does not forbid] until it imparts flavour to the gravy, the spices and the pieces
Rebbi: R' Yehuda's words appear [correct] where he did not stir and did not cover
